abstract: Virgo is a gravitational wave antenna aiming at the detection of gravitational waves emitted by astrophysical sources in a frequency range comprised between 10 Hz and a few kHz. The detector design and its present status are presented.

articleTitle: Path entangled photons from parametric down-conversion
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using stimulated parametric down-conversion, we propose a method for generating multiphoton path entanglement. By a special coincidence detection at one down-converted arm, the photons of the second arm non-locally bunch into the desired state. Experimental demonstration for the case of two photons is presented, as well as how to extend the scheme to any number of photons.

articleTitle: Coulomb-induced structure in the intersubband spectra of quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We predict extra features in the inter-subband absorption due a combination of many-body effects with the strong dipole moment k-dependence and valence band nonparabolicity of quantum wells.

articleTitle: Techniques for Reflectance-Based Determination of Optical Properties in Highly Attenuating Turbid Media
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Optical property measurement accuracy was evaluated for fiberoptic reflectance system with linear-array and bifurcated-fiber probes. A combined approach yielded a 75% reduction in errors for absorption and reduced scattering coefficients as compared to our previous system

articleTitle: Quantum magic mirror and imaging
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We experimentally show that chaotic light can behave as a "magic" mirror producing real images using second order correlation measurements. A ghost imaging scheme using the "magic" mirror is demonstrated and possible applications are discussed.

articleTitle: Inter-subband exciton relaxation dynamics in single-walled carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study inter-subband exciton relaxation dynamics in semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes with sub-30-fs temporal resolution. We measure a 40-fs time constant for energy relaxation from the second to the first excitonic transition.

articleTitle: Homogeneous broadening in quantum dots due to Auger scattering with wetting layer carriers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The homogeneous broadening in quantum dots due to various Auger scattering processes is calculated, accounting for exchange and screening. Many confined hole levels are required to obtain agreement with recent experimental results.

articleTitle: CW-pumped evanescent amplification at 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelength using highly Er/sup 3+/-doped glass over side-polished fiber
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A diode-pumped relative gain of 2 dB at 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelength based on evanescent excitation using a highly Er/sup 3+/-doped laser glass over side-polished fiber was demonstrated for the first time. The pump efficiency can be highly improved with a blazed grating to achieve ultra-low-noise fiber amplifiers and upconversion fiber lasers.

articleTitle: Quantization of the electromagnetic field in dispersive and absorptive structured dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a canonical Hamiltonian formulation for electromagnetic fields in dispersive and absorptive inhomogeneous structured dielectrics obeying the Kramers-Kronig relations. We present an effective band description of the polariton modes in the absorption band.

articleTitle: Tunable fiber laser using electroholography
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A tunable fiber laser composed of an EDFA ring resonator and an electroholographic switching element is presented. Tunability is accomplished by electric field multiplexing of volume holograms. The performance envelope of two architectures is discussed.

articleTitle: Dissipative Bragg solitons in thin film waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The dynamics of electromagnetic fields in photonic crystal waveguides pumped from the top is studied using a coupled mode approximation. The stability of the spatially uniform state and the formation of dissipative solitons are investigated.

articleTitle: Vortex interaction with a two-dimensional soliton lattice
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study experimentally and theoretically the nonlinear interaction between a vortex beam and a soliton lattice. We observe the vortex-induced lattice deformation and lattice twisting due to transfer of angular momentum carried by the vortex beam.

articleTitle: Dynamical investigation of internal field in LiNbO/sub 3/ crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate the defect-induced internal field in lithium niobate. By means of a full-field interferometric technique, a different electro-optic behaviour in opposite ferroelectric domains is observed due to an elastic component of internal field.

articleTitle: Hong-Ou-Mandel correlations using the zero-phonon-line emission of a single molecule
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We perform coincidence-counting experiments at the output of a Michelson interferometer using the zero-phonon-line emission of a single terrylenediimide molecule at 1.4 K. Under cw excitation, Hong-Ou-Mandel correlations are observed as the proof of two-photon interference.

articleTitle: Quantum wells intermixing in InGaAsP/InGaAsP laser structure for photonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the selective area bandgap tuning of multiple quantum well structures by an impurity free vacancy induced quantum well intermixing technique. A 3 dB waveguide directional coupler was fabricated in the disordered section of an intermixed quantum well sample as a demonstration of photonic device applications.

articleTitle: Far-field quantum statistics of light generated by a collection of two-level atoms
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study quantum statistics of optical fields in the far zone of a light source consisting of a number of uncorrelated atoms. The quantum statistics of such a system can be universal under certain conditions.

articleTitle: Direct measurement of photonic band structures by second harmonic generation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: By exploiting the phase sensitivity of second harmonic generation, we measure photonic band structures in PLLN waveguide arrays. Furthermore, we show that the concept can be applied to other photonic structures, as, e.g., photonic crystals.

articleTitle: High-power slab coupled optical waveguide laser (SCOWL) arrays
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: High-power 915-nm and 980-nm AlGaAs/InGaAs/GaAs single-spatial mode slab-coupled optical waveguide (SCOWL) laser diode arrays are described. Quasi-CW output powers of 100 W and CW output powers of 49 W have been demonstrated in single bars.

articleTitle: Laser Pulse Compression in Plasma Using Coherent Raman Cascade
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Compressing laser beams in plasmas via coherent Raman sideband generation is proposed. Electron density perturbations driven by the laser beatwave broaden the laser spectrum. Thus chirped laser beatnotes are compressed in plasma with high group velocity dispersion

articleTitle: Robust nonlinear chiral responses from gold nanoparticle arrays
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Strong chiral responses from arrays of L-shaped gold nanoparticles are observed through second-harmonic circular dichroism and tensor measurements. Comparisons suggest that small-scale defects are the primary source of broken symmetry which makes the samples chiral.

articleTitle: Efficient polarization squeezing as a resource for quantum communication
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on a novel and efficient source of polarization squeezing using a single pass through an optical fiber. Simply passing this Kerr squeezed beam through a carefully aligned /spl lambda//2 waveplate and splitting it on a polarization beam splitter, we find polarization squeezing of up to 5.1/spl plusmn/0.3 dB. The experimental setup allows for the direct measurement of the squeezing angle.

articleTitle: Polariton Propagation in Shallow-Confinement Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Polariton effects are studied by use of a microscopic theory. Linear and nonlinear transmission spectra are calculated with microscopic boundary conditions for the exciton and biexciton motion in ZnSe/ZnSSe-heterostructures. A direct theory-experiment comparison is presented

articleTitle: Quantum interference of electron de Broglie waves within a single molecule
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We measured ion and harmonic signals from aligned molecules as a function of the pump-probe delay. The observed anticorrelation between the two signals is the first demonstration of quantum interference of electron de Broglie waves.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Observed in Two-photon Transitions of K2
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Electromagetically Induced Transparency (EIT) has been observed in K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>two-photon transitions using a single laser. The intermediate mixed state A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>Σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>∼b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>Π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>resonantly enhanced the two-photon 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>Π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>→X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>Σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>transition.

articleTitle: Compact airborne aerosol lidar system
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A compact 532 nm and 1064 nm aerosol lidar has been deployed for small aircraft and ground based atmospheric measurements. Analog and photon counting detection are used to provide high resolution 3-D profiles over the Atlantic Ocean.

articleTitle: Extended InGaAs/InGaAs quantum structures for near infrared photodetection beyond 1.9 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Extended InGaAs quantum structures were grown on InP substrate using two strain compensation techniques by molecular beam epitaxy. The material quality was characterized and the absorption coefficient was measured with transmission spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Two-photon absorption and the dispersion of nonlinear refraction using a white-light continuum Z-scan
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We use white-light continuum Z-scan to measure the degenerate two-photon absorption spectrum and associated dispersion of the nonlinear refraction, n/sub 2/, of ZnSe/spl middot/n/sub 2/ changes sign at around 0.7 of the bandgap energy as predicted.

articleTitle: Efficient generation of a three-photon W state
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A three-photon W state was generated with 30 times higher efficiency and 10 times lower pump power than a previous work by utilizing weak coherent light. The scheme can be naturally extended to higher order.

articleTitle: Fiber-amplifier based THz source using difference-frequency generation in a DAST crystal
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A passively Q-switched Cr/sup 4+/:Nd/sup 3+/:YAG microchiplaser is amplified in an Yb-fiber. The occurring sidemodes are used for THz-generation in a DAST crystal. These first investigations show quasi cw output powers in the order of 0.2 nW.

articleTitle: High-speed, amplified, frequency swept laser at 20 kHz sweep rates for OCT imaging
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a high-speed, frequency swept, 1300 nm laser for Fourier domain OCT. The laser generates ~45 mW instantaneous power with 20 kHz sweep rates and achieves 108 dB sensitivity and 12.7 mum resolution

articleTitle: CEO phase-locked 5.7-fs pulses through filamentation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Self-compression of a CEO phase-locked 43 fs, 0.84 mJ pulse during filamentation leads to a CFO-phase locked 5.7-fs, 0.38-mJ pulse with an excellent spatial mode. The obtained pulse bandwidth exceeds 600 THz theoretically 1.8-fs pulses.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Microscopy by Selective Illumination with Feedback
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A novel method of 3D microscopy is demonstrated based on illumination of an object by a processed image of itself in a feedback loop. Using a simple apparatus, we obtain 8 mum optical sectioning resolution

articleTitle: Probing electron dynamics in single-wall carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Photoexcited single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) have been examined by time-resolved fluorescence measurements. Non-radiative relaxation on a 10-ps scale was observed, as well as a faster Auger process for SWNTs containing multiple electron-hole pairs.

articleTitle: Linear optical quantum computation with parity encoding
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a linear optics quantum computation scheme that employs an incremental parity encoding approach. The scheme uses techniques from cluster state computation and achieves comparable resource usage with increased tolerance to photon loss.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy of francium: lifetime measurement of the 8s level and investigations of cold collisions
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present spectroscopic investigations of francium that include the measurement of the lifetime of the 8s level and photoassociation spectroscopy to look at the formation of francium molecules.

articleTitle: Neodymium random laser with external mirrors
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We studied the dependence of neodymium random laser emission on external mirrors and thickness of the powder layer. The major observed trends and recommendations for optimization of the random laser output are presented.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh-Q nanocavity based on photonic-crystal double heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate that a double heterostructure in a two-dimensional photonic-crystal slab is crucial for the strong confinement of photons in volumes of optical-wavelength size. An extremely high quality factor over 2.7/spl times/10/sup 5/ has been achieved experimentally.

articleTitle: Low-voltage operation photodetector made by coupling superlattice and quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have investigated a novel photodetector structure of coupling superlattice and quantum wells. This device can be operated at low bias range and even the photovoltaic mode. The broadband response is achieved by this structure.

articleTitle: Periodic structures produced by a scanning beam of a femtosecond Ti:sapphire laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The formation of periodic ripples due to the interference of a scanning beam of a femtosecond Ti:sapphire laser with a surface electromagnetic wave is reported in several solids (Ge, GaAs, W, etc.) exposed in air.

articleTitle: Optical ratchet resonators
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present novel "ratchet" resonators. Due to dynamical localization of resonant modes and broken symmetry between positive and negative angular momenta, these devices show increased efficiency of light trapping and can be used for sensing applications.

articleTitle: Control of Laser Pulses Shape Using Coherent Population Trapping
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In the paper we show how can control temporal shape of laser pulses using the phenomenon of a coherent population trapping (CPT). Temporal compression is demonstrated as a special case of pulse tailoring,. In addition, it is discussed manipulating of a temporal shape of retrieved pulse recorded on basis of CPT.

articleTitle: Saturated high-repetition soft X-ray lasers at wavelengths down to 13.9 nm in Ni-like ions
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Saturated tabletop lasers between 18.9 and 13.9 nm operating at 5 Hz repetition rate are demonstrated from Nickel-like transitions. The results were obtained utilizing a picosecond laser heating pulse of only 1 J.

articleTitle: Radiation efficiency of water-window Cherenkov sources using atomic shell resonances
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We developed simple theory of Cherenkov radiation at atomic resonances in the X-ray water window for L-shells in 5 trans-oxigen elements and proposed K-shell resonance in liquid nitrogen. Our results compare favorably with experimental data

articleTitle: Bremsstrahlung radiation from the ultraintense field ionization of atoms
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Atomic ionization in a 10/sup 17/ W/cm/sup 2/ to 10/sup 20/ W/cm/sup 2/ laser focus is analyzed using a semi-classical ensemble model. We present the energy and angle resolved photoionization and bremsstrahlung radiation out to 10 MeV at 10/sup 20/ W/cm/sup 2/.

articleTitle: FCS for characterizing nano-optical systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Many groups have performed detailed calculations of the electromagnetic distribution near nanostructures for optical applications. Fluorescence correlation spectroscopy is a powerful experimental tool for validating these calculations and the effectiveness of nanostructures.

articleTitle: Molecular alignment effects on high harmonic generation in N/sub 2/ in a hollow core waveguide
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Nitrogen molecules in a capillary waveguide are transiently aligned using intense laser pulses. Significant variations in the HHG yield are observed as the molecular axis direction is varied with respect to the polarization an intense probe laser.

articleTitle: Parametric down-conversion of higher-order Bessel beams in nonlinear crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: It is revealed that orbital angular momentum can be conserved within the spontaneous parametric down-conversion of higher-order Bessel beam. A qualitative agreement of theoretical predictions with experimental results is obtained.

articleTitle: Current status of TAMA300 interferometer
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The current status of the TAMA300 laser interferometer is reviewed here. We started operation of the TAMA300 detector in 1099, and are now collecting and analyzing observational data to search for gravitational wave signals.

articleTitle: Reliability of the beamsplitter based Bell-state measurement
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A linear 50/50 beamsplitter, together with a coincidence measurement, has been widely used in quantum optical experiments, such as teleportation, dense coding, etc., for interferometrically distinguishing, measuring, or projecting onto one of the four two-photon polarization Bell-states |/spl Psi//sup (-)/>. In this paper, we demonstrate that the coincidence measurement at the output of a beamsplitter cannot be used as an absolute identifier of the input state |/spl Psi//sup (-)/> nor as an indication that the input photons have projected to the |/spl Psi//sup (-)/> state.

articleTitle: Dark hollow laser beam based neutral atom beam switch and divider
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the first demonstration of neutral atom beam switches and dividers, created with crossed dark hollow laser beams generated with a two-dimensional spatial light modulator.

articleTitle: Wide tuning characteristics and passive mode-locking of a Ce/sup 3+/-Er/sup 3+/-ZBLAN fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Wide tuning over 120 nm and passive mode locking of a Ce/sup 3+/-Er/sup 3+/-ZBLAN fiber laser by a semiconductor saturable-absorber is described for the first time. A Q-switched mode-locked output was obtained with 400 MHz repetition rate.

articleTitle: Externally driven defects in photonic crystal slabs
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate that an external holding beam compensates for losses of a defect mode in a PC-slab. We obtain a considerable field enhancement, an injection of light into the PC-structures and enhanced nonlinear effects.

articleTitle: Tuning (multiplying) the channel density of optical frequency combs by cross-phase-modulation in fibers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In this paper, it is demonstrated that spectral-domain Talbot effects can be induced on frequency combs by in-fiber cross-phase-modulation with a Gaussian pump pulse. The comb free-spectral-range can be reduced (by any integer factor) by simply adjusting the pump peak power.

articleTitle: 1D nano-ultrasonic scan with 1-nanometer spatial resolution
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Piezoelectric quantum wells can be treated as opto-acoustic transducers to generate and detect acoustic waves with nanometer wavelengths. This opto-acoustic transducer was utilized for 1D ultrasonic scan with 1 nanometer demonstrated resolution.

articleTitle: Highly efficient quasi-two-level 901 nm laser emission of Nd/sup 3+/ in strontium lanthanum aluminate
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Highly efficient, 0.84 slope efficiency quasi-two-level 901 nm emission is reported for Nd/sup 3+/ in lanthanum strontium aluminate by Ti:sapphire laser pumping at 865 nm.

articleTitle: Incoherent solitons and condensation processes
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that coherent phase effects may play a relevant role in the nonlinear propagation of partially incoherent waves, which lead to unexpected processes of condensation, or incoherent soliton generation in instantaneous response nonlinear media.

articleTitle: High-frequency response of electro-optic single crystal KTa/sub x/Nb/sub 1-x/O/sub 3/ in paraelectric phase
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Electro-optic constants of KTa/sub x/Nb/sub 1-x/O/sub 3/ can be up to 600 pm/V with a bias voltage. In this report, dielectric dispersion is investigated to examine the electro-optic effect in a 1 MHz to 3 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Submicron-resolution optical coherence tomography using noncollinear parametric down-conversion
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Submicron axial resolution in optical coherence tomography is demonstrated using one output beam from a broadband noncollinear parametric down-conversion source. The large spectral bandwidth is achieved by tightly focusing the narrowband pump laser.

articleTitle: Implementation of a novel self-heterodyne filtering method by wavelength shift keying modulation for optical CDMA
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose and implement a new method of optical CDMA based on self-heterodyne filtering. Unlike most CDMA systems no spectrum spreading is required, thus enabling long-reach transmission capability.

articleTitle: The one- and two-photon transverse wave functions: theory and experiment
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a method to characterize one- and two-photon transverse wave functions in coordinate space. Measurements of transverse Wigner functions for one- and two-photon states from a spontaneous parametric down conversion source are being made.

articleTitle: The position dependence of nitrogen in BAC model with 10 band Hamiltonian: band mixing effects and gain in InGaNAs/GaAs quantum well lasers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An improved band anti-crossing model is presented in which the position of the nitrogen within the quantum well is included. This is found to strongly influence the conduction band levels, the dipole moments and gain.

articleTitle: Decoherence of CW random lasers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Measurements of output power and spatial coherence length versus excitation rate of an electrically-pumped alumina random laser are compared with conventional laser equations and one-dimensional modeling to test the consistency of quenching and decoherence behavior.

articleTitle: Interpreting learning control of molecular fragmentation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This presentation will focus on progress toward uncovering the physical mechanisms underlying control in a series of closed loop molecular fragmentation experiments using shaped ultrafast laser pulses.

articleTitle: Optically stimulated and spontaneously generated electron spin coherence in quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the observation of long-lived quantum beats in quantum dots (ensemble and single) due to electron spin coherence, resulting from stimulated Raman transition as well as spontaneous radiative decay of the trion state.

articleTitle: Parametric Six-Wave Mixing and Quantum Beating at 608 cm-1in Rb
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Parametric six-wave mixing is achieved in Rb and quantum beating at 608 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is investigated at different Rb number densities by observing coherent radiation at 495 nm produced by summing the pump and the signal

articleTitle: Molecular structure effects on high harmonic generation in CO/sub 2/
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study the harmonic orders 25-47 from field-free aligned CO/sub 2/ as a function of time-delay between the alignment and HHG pulse. Harmonic-order dependent enhancement (decrease) of high-harmonic yield for aligned (anti-aligned) time-delays is observed.

articleTitle: Observation of coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering in phase-mismatched direction
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have experimentally demonstrated CARS scattering in the forward and backward directions. The signal observed in the backscattered is of the orders of magnitude stronger than would be expected.

articleTitle: Interferometry for space-based gravitational wave detection
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will be the first space-based laser interferometric gravitational wave detector. LISA poses a new set of challenges, requiring picometer level interferometric measurements between spacecraft separated by 5 million kilometers.

articleTitle: Experimental study of the momentum correlation of a pseudo-thermal field in the photon counting regime
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Thermal radiation has been recently proposed for imaging and interference experiments to simulate entangled state. We report an experimental study on the momentum correlation properties of a pseudo-thermal field in the photon counting regime.

articleTitle: Accurate Sampling of Gaussian Laser Beam Profile in Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We find an accurate probability density function for Monte Carlo sampling of a Gaussian laser beam, which can be used to accurately model light transport in tissue. It is shown that our proposed method is accurate by comparing to the exact solution made by the convolution.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh Resolution, Functional OCT with All-Fiber Broadband Raman-Continuum Light-Source
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Coherent, spectral and intensity noise of a CW-pumped broadband Raman-continuum light source is determined for functional, ultrahigh resolution OCT. First application results to functional ultrahigh-resolution (3.5 mum) OCT for probing of retinal physiology are presented

articleTitle: Ultrafast dynamics of nonlinear excitations in quasi-one-dimensional systems probed by time-resolved THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present time-resolved spectroscopic studies of the evolution of charge carriers and localized nonlinear excitations in a quasi-one-dimensional molecular system using femtosecond time-resolved THz techniques.

articleTitle: Nonclassical-light generation in a photonic band-gap nonlinear planar waveguide
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A nonlinear planar photonic band-gap waveguide with optical parametric process can be used as a source of squeezed light and light with sub-Poissonian photon-number statistics. Suitable conditions for nonclassical-light generation are specified.

articleTitle: A simple and fast technique to characterize the group delay properties of fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A novel method that uses a simple and fast iterative algorithm to recover the group delay of any fiber Bragg grating from its measured transmission spectrum is described. Its benefits over leading techniques in this field are much greater speed, simplicity, and high accuracy even in the presence of significant experimental noise.

articleTitle: Negative refractive index in a right-handed medium
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Our theoretical analysis shows that the refractive index may be negative in a homogeneous isotropic non-magnetic medium with positive electric permittivity. This provides a possible route to negative refraction at optical frequencies.

articleTitle: Observation of 2/sup nd/ band vortex-ring soliton in 2D photonic lattices
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the first observation of second-band vortex-ring solitons in 2D photonic lattices, along with a theoretical study of their stability. This constitutes the first observation of a 2D higher-band lattice soliton.

articleTitle: Harmonic generation characteristics of QPM quartz in visible-to-UV region
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report SHG properties in QPM quartz. Temperature bandwidth of 32.7/spl deg/C cm at 1064 nm was obtained and wavelength dependence of QPM period was measured for designing UV generator with higher-order QPM by Ti:Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ laser.

articleTitle: Coincident-frequency entanglement via extended phase matching
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a source of entangled photon pairs with identical frequency spectra. An Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometric measurement of this source shows a high visibility of 85% under pulsed pumping and without any spectral filtering.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical response of two coupled semiconductor quantum dots: differential transmission spectra
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A theoretical description of the ultrafast nonlinear optical response of two coupled quantum dots including interdot Coulomb coupling and electron-phonon interaction is given. We discuss the observability of the coupling effects in differential transmission spectra.

articleTitle: Measurement of the spectral properties of the two-photon state generated via type-II spontaneous parametric down-conversion
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the complete measurement of the spectral properties of photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. The measurements, which include not only single-photon spectra, but also two-photon joint spectra, were performed for both cw and ultrafast pumping configurations. In agreement with theoretical predictions, the spectra for the ultrafast pumped case reveal asymmetries not present with cw pumping.

articleTitle: 10 GHz amplified feedback lasers with a wide frequency-tuning range
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Monolithic amplified feedback semiconductor lasers with a wide frequency-tuning range are presented as a solution to 10 GHz optical pulsation, which reduce the necessity for precise control of a cavity length.

articleTitle: X-Ray Generation from Metal Targets Coated with Wavelength-Scale Spheres
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: X-ray yield measurements from targets coated with wavelength-scale spheres are compared with measurements from polished targets. Evidence for a hotter resonant electron temperature due to field enhancements from Mie resonances in the spheres is investigated

articleTitle: Coherent control of two-photon phenomena with broadband nonclassical light
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report two control experiments that exploit the coherent correlations within the spectrum of incoherent broadband down-converted light to demonstrate ultrahigh spectral and temporal resolutions at high power and inherent non-classical features at low power.

articleTitle: Single color injection of ballistic spin-polarized currents in strained [110]-oriented GaAs quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Spin-polarized ballistic charge currents are generated in strained GaAs with single 60 fs optical pulses and detected via THz experiments. State filling and carrier-dependent momentum scattering lead to a sublinear intensity dependence at high pump intensities.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal X Waves in Highly Nonlinear Optical Systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The formation of spatiotemporal X waves is investigated in planar highly nonlinear normally dispersive AlGaAs waveguides. The roles of the amplitude and relative phase of a CW background on a bell-shaped spatiotemporal beam are considered

articleTitle: Cross-shell multielectron ionization of xenon by an ultrastrong laser field
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Strong field ionization measurements of xenon from 10/sup 13/ W/cm/sup 2/ to 10/sup 18/ W/cm/sup 2/ show enhanced rescattering ionization for charge states as high as Xe/sup +10/ and a multiphoton/tunneling ionization character dictated by the Kepler orbit time.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of nonlinear optical loop mirrors in chirped fiber gratings compensated dispersion-managed transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that nonlinear optical loop mirrors can dramatically suppress the side peaks induced by the group delay ripples in chirped fiber gratings compensated dispersion-managed systems and significantly improve the system performance.

articleTitle: Phase-compensated ultra-bright source of entangled photons
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: By compensating for a phase-based decoherence effect, we produce the brightest high quality source of polarization entangled photons to date: 2.01*10/sup 6/ measured pairs per second.

articleTitle: Transparency oscillations in avalanche upconversion
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Electromagnetically-induced transparency is shown to exhibit transient pulsations in active upconversion solids. Density matrix solutions predict that an avalanche upconversion laser assisted by EIT can be self-starting under certain conditions. We examine prospects for high power operation in Tm:LiYF/sub 4/.

articleTitle: Terahertz generation in poled polymers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: THz radiation power dependence on pump laser spot size was explored using a poled polymer and the electro-optic coefficient of the polymer was estimated. THz spectroscopy on several UV-curable passive polymers was also carried out.

articleTitle: Carrier envelope phase effects on electron quantum paths in high harmonics generation by few-cycle pulses
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: High-order harmonic spectra generated by few-optical-cycle pulses have been acquired on a single-shot basis. We show that the differences in the generated spectra are related to variations in the electron-quantum-paths contributing to the emission process.

articleTitle: Real time 3D nonlinear microscopy
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a nonlinear microscope scheme being capable of simultaneous, 3D investigation of the electric activity pattern of neural networks or signal summation rules of individual neurons in a 0.6times0.6times0.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> volume with sub-micrometer spatial resolution

articleTitle: Conductivity of single-walled carbon nanotubes probed by THz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: THz time-domain spectroscopy is applied to probe the transient conductivity single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs). The ultrafast transport properties and carrier dynamics are examined for different levels of laser excitation.

articleTitle: Entanglement manipulation with linear optics
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Entanglement extraction is a first-step application of the linear-optics quantum-information processing. It is useful in distributing entanglement via realistic noisy transmission lines. In the talk I will present the principle, experiment, and further possible applications.

articleTitle: Non-magnetic left-handed composite
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a new approach to systems with negative index of refraction. The proposed design is non-magnetic and scalable from GHz to optical frequencies. We describe optical properties of the proposed structure and its realizations.

articleTitle: Efficient 355-nm generation in high-quality CsB/sub 3/O/sub 5/ fabricated by post-growth heat treatments
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Post-growth heat treatments of CsB/sub 3/O/sub 5/ enable to produce high-quality optical devices free from scattering centers. It has generated 14-W UV radiation at 355 nm, which is three times higher than that obtained by LiB/sub 3/O/sub 5/.

articleTitle: Enhancement of resonant Raman scattering from ZnO quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Efficient resonant Raman scattering (RRS) were observed in ZnO quantum dots (ZnO-QDs). The size dependent shift of UV-emission reveals quantum confinement governs the enhancement of RRS through modifying the phonon state density in ZnO-QDs.

articleTitle: Novel multi-channel optical carrier suppression technique for wavelength division multiplexed systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A polarization modulator generates an optical spectrum in which the carrier and fundamental sidebands are orthogonally polarized. A polarizer is used to selectively suppress the carrier. A carrier suppression of /spl sim/36 dB is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Time evolution of entanglement: an example in cavity QED
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate theoretically and experimentally entanglement in a weakly driven cavity QED system with correlation functions commonly encountered in quantum optics.

articleTitle: All optical RZ to NRZ format conversion using phase modulation in a dispersion-shifted fiber
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate two schemes for return-to-zero to non-return-to-zero format conversion using spectral broadening caused by nonlinear phase modulation in a dispersion-shifted fiber. Less then 2 dB power penalty has been observed in both conversion schemes.

articleTitle: Low threshold extended cavity lasers through two-stage laser-induced intermixing
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Low loss intermixed passive waveguides were achieved through a two-stage laser-induced quantum well intermixing process. Low threshold current extended cavity lasers that consist of passive intermixed waveguides and active laser sources were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Microfocus Cu-Kαsource for femtosecond x-ray science
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demostrate a sub-picosecond 1-kHz femtosecond X-ray source (flux: 5times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> photons/s) with a well accessible quasi-point size (10 mum diameter) providing Cu K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">alpha</sub> emission in continuous operation (10 hours), which we use to characterize two different types of focusing optics

articleTitle: Observation of optical gain in InAs nanocrystals embedded in a polymer matrix
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We developed a new material platform that enables inclusion of InAs nanocrystals, emitting at 1.55 microns, into a transparent polymer matrix while preserving their optical properties. Three beam, time resolved pump-probe measurements show signatures of optical gain in InAs nanocrystals for the first time.

articleTitle: Enhanced optical fields and mixing of trapped plasmons in reproducibly engineered spherical nano-cavities
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Metal nano-scale spherical voids embedded in thin films exhibit strong plasmon resonances that are tuneable using structural parameters of our 3D assembly process. Localised void plasmons possessing large field enhancements strongly couple to incident light.

articleTitle: Photothermal heterodyne imaging and spectroscopy of individual metal nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We introduce a highly sensitive far-field optical method for imaging individual non-fluorescent nano-objects. This allows for the unprecedented detection of individual gold clusters of only 67 atoms. The spectroscopy of individual nanoclusters is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Squeezing enhancement due to localization of light in PBG nonlinear waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study a 1D photonic band-gap nonlinear device as an optical parametric oscillator. We find that squeezed light generation is enhanced with respect to a bulk, exploiting the localization effect of this structure.

articleTitle: Superluminal light propagation through a diode-pumped Nd:YVO4crystal
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The group velocity of optical pulse in an amplifier in the presence of population oscillations was studied both theoretically and experimentally. The superluminal propagation of harmonically modulated light was measured in a diode-pumped Nd:YVO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>crystal.

articleTitle: Above-threshold double ionization of helium with attosecond intense soft X-ray pulses
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We theoretically study above-threshold double ionization of helium by attosecond, intense high-order harmonic pulses. Whereas the two electrons are ejected sequentially, the ionization interval is so short that they can exchange energy.

articleTitle: Resonant and off-resonant two-color Raman solitons in gas filled photonic band-gap fibres
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report numerical investigation of propagation of two-color temporal solitons supported by Raman nonlinearity in the gas filled hollow-core photonic crystal fibres. We investigate solitons tuned close to and detuned far from the Raman resonance.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of high dimensional time-energy entangled two-photon states
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Two-photon states generated in parametric down-conversion are shown to exhibit D-dimensional discretized energy-time entanglement, where D is possibly as large as half a million. Additionally a three-order-of-magnitude violation of the classical variance product is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Green light generation in periodically poled Zn doped LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguides fabricated by He+-implantation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Green laser generation by using quasi-phase-matching is investigated in helium implanted periodically poled Zn doped lithium niobate waveguides.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of the nonlinear optical loop mirror with low-birefringence, twisted fiber
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We measure the transmission characteristics of the nonlinear optical loop mirror with a polarization asymmetry. Simple polarization adjustments enable the nonlinear control of the transmission for applications such as pedestal suppression, amplitude regularization, and mode-locking.

articleTitle: Multielectron ionization of Ne/sup +n/ in ultrastrong laser fields: rescattering and the role of the magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Neon ionization measurements from 10/sup 14/W/cm/sup 2/ to 10/sup 18/W/cm/sup 2/ quantify rescattering and nonsequential ionization physics as the interaction evolves from a nonrelativistic to relativistic response. A relativistic 3D model is found to be in excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Tomography of Animal Tissues by Digital Interference Holography
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The digital interference holography is applied to imaging bovine muscle and other tissues. Three dimensional micro-tomographic images are obtained with 1 micron lateral and 10 micron axial resolution and 1.5 mm penetration.

articleTitle: Single-photon switches for quantum information processing
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Recent work towards the realization of low-loss, high-speed, optical switches designed to accommodate single photon qubits is discussed. Preliminary results from an all-optical switch and plans for an electro-optical switch are described.

articleTitle: Dispersion-guided and bandgap-guided resonances in semiconductor waveguide-coupled hexagonal photonic-crystal-embedded microcavities
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report dispersion-guided resonances and bandgap-guided resonances in semiconductor waveguide-coupled hexagonal photonic-crystal-embedded microcavities. Our two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain simulations reveal highly efficient coupled high-Q resonances in both types of resonances.

articleTitle: Controlling spontaneous emission rate in solid state for quantum information science
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We enhance and suppress the excitonic lifetime of an InAs quantum dot (QD) by modifying its alignment with a resonance cavity in a photonic crystal slab. The QD/cavity system has applications in quantum information science.

articleTitle: Analysis of implantation induced gratings for CWDM
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The Bragg reflection coefficients suitable for a CWDM system have been calculated by using coupled mode theory based on perturbation obtained by impurity induced intermixing of quantum wells and analyzed for different order gratings.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic apertureless near-field optical microscope
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate apertureless near-field optical imaging with material contrast on metal nanostructures, by local second-harmonic generation at a metal tip properly illuminated at grazing incidence by femtosecond pulses.

articleTitle: Broadband THz response of a resonantly excited high-density exciton gas
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The density-driven crossover of electron-hole pairs from insulating to conducting states is observed via the internal 1s-2p exciton resonance. Decreasing interparticle distance induces strong shifts and broadening, and ultimately the disappearance of the excitonic resonance.

articleTitle: Wavelength dependence of the fast photoresponse of nanographite films
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate that a strong light-induced electric signal generated in nanographite reproduces shape of nanosecond light pulses in the interval 260-5000 nm. This indicates that nanographite can be employed in ultrafast light detectors.

articleTitle: Spectral phase characterization of a 40 GHz self-pulsating DBR laser based on intensity autocorrelation analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a self-referenced method to measure the phase difference between longitudinal modes in self-pulsating lasers with high frequency repetition rate based on autocorrelation analysis of groups of three adjacent longitudinal modes.

articleTitle: Relativistic ultra-gradient non-potential force: electron-laser energy transfer and laser gate for electrons
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In contrast to the Kapitsa-Dirac gradient force conserving the energy of electron beam crossing a laser beam, our theory shows large energy transfer between them in the relativistic case, if L-beam has steep gradient

articleTitle: Electronic shell structure in single InAs/InGaAs quantum dots emitting at 1.3 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Photoluminescence spectra from single In(Ga)As:Bi quantum dots in a quantum well show low-temperature emission around 1300 nm. We observe the formation of neutral and charged exciton complexes and a large s-p shell splitting.

articleTitle: Acousto-Optic Tunable Filter-Based Near Infrared Spectro-Polarimeter for Polymer Rheology
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An acousto-optic tunable filter and photo-elastic polarization state modulator-based near infrared spectropolarimeter was built for measuring rheological functions of polymers. Measurement of sample linear birefringence and dichroism agree with literature and other independent test.

articleTitle: Dynamics of the inter-Landau-level magnetoplasmon coherence in a quantum Hall system
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We use three-pulse four-wave mixing spectroscopy to observe coherent femtosecond dynamics of collective nanoscale excitations in the quantum Hall regime. We observe interference effects of the inter Landau level magnetoplasmon coherence and study its dephasing.

articleTitle: Dependence of multiple filamentation on beam ellipticity
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We experimentally investigate the effects of beam ellipticity on multiple filamentation. For high ellipticities the beam breaks into bands and filaments as the power is increased, and numerical simulations are in qualitative agreement.

articleTitle: In-reservoir coherent control of the atom-photon bound state
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the collective operator master equation for bosonic reservoirs with gaps in the density of photonic states. We show that the atom-photon bound state can be produced and controlled by the in-reservoir coherent field.

articleTitle: Laser-Driven and E-Beam Driven Plasma Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This paper is a research on the interaction between intense particle beams and lasers with plasmas. Interestingly, the focused intensity (or energy density) of the state-of-the-art particle beams and lasers are both ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. At these intensities the space charge fields or the beam and the fields of the laser are large enough to rapidly accelerate plasma electrons to relativistic energies and are high enough to tunnel ionize a gas. It is also fundamental to the field of plasma-based accelerators

articleTitle: Polarization control with two-dimensional coupled photonic crystal microcavity arrays
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We measured band diagrams of two-dimensional coupled-photonic crystal microcavity arrays and obtained group velocity below 0.008c. A strong polarization sensitivity is observed with rotationally asymmetric structures, which can be used in polarizing mirrors and sensors.

articleTitle: Measurement and modeling of two-photon absorption spectrum in azoaromatic compounds
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This work reports a systematic study on the degenerate two-photon absorption spectrum of azo-aromatic compounds, using the Z-scan technique with femtosecond pulses. The nonlinear spectra obtained were modeled using a perturbation theory treatment.

articleTitle: Optically pumping the spin of a single quantum dot
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: I will discuss Hanle and Overhauser experiments demonstrating the optical pumping of electron and nuclear spin in individual charged quantum dots.

articleTitle: Comparison of the nonlinear transmission of Cd/sub 0.65/Mg/sub 0.35/Te and CdTe
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The nonlinear absorption coefficient of magnesium doped cadmium telluride (Cd/sub 0.65/Mg/sub 0.35/Te) is measured and compared with undoped CdTe. The samples were tested at 1064 nm using both picosecond and nanosecond lasers.

articleTitle: Phase matching, quasi phase matching and pulse compression in a single waveguide for enhancing high harmonic generation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate enhancement of high harmonic generation in the technologically significant 95 eV photon energy region by combining phase matching, quasi phase matching, and pulse compression in a single gas-filled waveguide. The waveguide geometry allows us to use argon gas as the generating medium, which also leads to enhanced emission due to its higher nonlinearity. The induced shock front due to laser pulse compression in the ionizing gas medium also generates an X-ray continuum at low pressure, with a spectrum corresponding to an isolated, 50 attosecond, X-ray pulse.

articleTitle: Laser radiometry for F/sub 2/ lasers at 157 nm
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: First results of the calibration of a commercially available thermal detector for 157 nm F/sub 2/ laser radiation at power levels around 700 mW are presented. The responsivity, homogeneity and uncertainties were investigated and determined.

articleTitle: To Improve CSO/CTB Performances by Using Polarization Modulation Technique
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A two-wavelength wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) CATV transport system that employed polarization modulation (PolM) technique to reduce the self-phase modulation (SPM) and crosstalk is proposed and demonstrated. In contrast to a two-wavelength WDM CATV transport system used intensity modulation (IM) technique, good performances of composite second order (CSO) and composite triple beat (CTB) were obtained accompanied by acceptable carrier-to-noise ratio (CNR) value in our proposed system over a 100-km single-mode fiber (SMF) transmission.

articleTitle: Theory of control of spin/photon interface for solid-state quantum network
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: With Dot-Cavity-Waveguide coupled system acting as quantum interface for stationary spin qubit and flying photon qubit, we propose and study a controlling scheme for generation or reception of an arbitrarily designated wavepacket of a single-photon.

articleTitle: Formation of ultracold ground-state RbCs via photoassociation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the Franck-Condon analysis of an efficient transition scheme to populate the ground lowest vibrational level of RbCs following photoassociation and report observation of ultracold RbCs molecules in a dual MOT by two-photon ionization.

articleTitle: Advances in nanophotonics: ultrafast & ultrasensitive
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In this tutorial on NanoPhotonics recent advances are highlighted with focus on near field optical methods, ultra-fast probing of single molecules and ultra-sensitive detection of individual non-fluorescent nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic generation on the nanoscale: new routes for surface and bulk investigations
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Second-harmonic generation from individual nanostructures is demonstrated. New symmetry selection rules derived for asymmetric nanoparticles allow for the distinction of different nonlinear source polarizations and enable simultaneous surface and bulk investigations.

articleTitle: Exciton-photon coupling in organic materials with large intersystem crossing rates and strong excited state molecular relaxation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We examine the influence of singlet-triplet intersystem crossing and excited state relaxation on exciton-photon coupling in small molecule organic optical microcavities. Both processes quench coupling under non-resonant excitation, allowing estimations of their relative transition rates.

articleTitle: Non-Gaussian optical field statistics in a long-haul soliton-based DPSK transmission system
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate with importance-sampled Monte-Carlo simulations that the tails of the optical field's probability distribution at the end of a long-haul soliton-based DPSK transmission system are strongly non-Gaussian.

articleTitle: Analysis of dilute nitride semiconductor laser gain materials in the 1.3-1.5 /spl mu/m range
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Theory/experiment comparisons of optical properties of dilute nitride heterostructures are presented. A type I - type II transition in In/sub 0.23/Ga/sub 0.77/As/GaN/sub x/As/sub 1-x/ heterostructures is identified. The model is used for a study of lasing in the 1.3-1.5 /spl mu/m range.

articleTitle: Observation of Relativistic Cross-Phase Modulation in High Intensity Laser-Plasma Interactions
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report a novel nonlinear optical phenomena, relativistic cross-phase modulation between Raman light and a high intensity laser pulse in an underdense plasma. The experimental spectra compared well with calculations from a proposed theoretical model

articleTitle: Optical spin injection from a ZnMnSe spin aligner into GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Spin-polarized excitons are optically created in a diluted magnetic semiconductor layer and transferred to a non-magnetic GaAs/AlGaAs quantum well. The photoluminescence intensity is measured polarization resolved and gives clear evidence for efficient spin injection.

articleTitle: Noise suppression in a novel monolithically integrated Michelson Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A novel monolithically integrated Micheson interferometer using intersecting twin-contact semiconductor optical amplifiers is proposed whereby the two arms are gain imbalanced to give noise suppression. Experimental OSNR improvement of 6.2 dB for 3 ps pulses is demonstrated

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a standalone Raman-based all-optical nanosensor
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have designed, fabricated and optimized an all-optical nanosensor that utilizes surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) combined with a molecular interface to selectively probe local, in vivo environments.

articleTitle: Coherent spin waves in thin-film GaMnAs
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using pump-probe techniques we study coherent magnons in the ferromagnetic semiconductor GaMnAs. The magnetic anisotropy and spin stiffness constants are determined from the magnetic-field dependence of the frequency of the standing spin waves.

articleTitle: Amplification of femtosecond filaments
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study the formation of femtosecond filaments in an amplifying medium (Ti:Sa). Subthreshold onset of filamentation as well as flux amplification without fragmentation is observed, in good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Conditions for spin squeezing in laser-cooled rubidium
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a scheme to generate spin squeezing via a quantum non-demolition (QND) measurement in a cold sample of /sup 87/Rb atoms using the 5S/sub 1/2 /(F=1) hyperfine ground state.

articleTitle: Phase Gates With Four-Level Inverted-Y System
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The four-level atomic system in inverted-Y configuration is investigated for large Kerr-nonlinearities. The cross-Kerr nonlinearities generated in such system can produce phase-shifts of order π and can be used for realizing polarization quantum phase gates.

articleTitle: Coherent lidar range processing of broadband optical noise waveforms
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present proof-of-concept results for coherent 'time-of-flight' lidar range processing of broadband analog optical noise waveforms using the spectral sensing material Tm:YAG. Time-of-flight resolution of /spl sim/450 ps with /spl sim/30 dB of signal-to-noise ratio is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Coupled-resonator optical waveguides (CROWs) doped with semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We explore nanocrystal-doped microsphere resonators as building blocks for coupled-resonator optical waveguides. The evolution of waveguide modes is studied using polarization-sensitive microphotoluminescence spectroscopy. We demonstrate the formation of linear waveguides and light-bending resonator arrays.

articleTitle: Experimental observation of the magnitude and sign of the third order optical nonlinearity in CdS quantum dots in a dendrimer matrix
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have investigated the nonlinear optical response of CdS quantum dots in a poly(propyleneimine) dendrimer matrix having diaminobutane (DAB) core. Large nonlinear coefficients and low absorption losses were observed at all wavelengths.

articleTitle: Experimental weak measurements in Hardy's Paradox
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Hardy's Paradox brings to light some of the striking difficulties in the interpretation of indirect quantum measurements. We weakly measure the location of the particles in Hardy's Paradox. The results provide a self-consistent resolution.

articleTitle: Highly flexible switching characteristic using nonlinear polarization rotation in a nonlinear optical loop mirror
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate theoretically that a wide variety of nonlinear switching characteristics can be obtained from a single NOLM structure exploiting nonlinear polarization rotation. Control parameters are the orientation of a wave plate and input polarization.

articleTitle: Autocorrelation measurement of sub 10-fs high-order harmonics at 42 eV
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In this paper, we report the pulse width measurement of the 27th harmonic having a photon energy of 42 eV, which is the highest photon energy inducing nonlinear process, by autocorrelation technique. The two-photon double ionization of He is used as the nonlinear process for autocorrelation. The pulse duration of 8 fs is obtained with the pump pulse of 20 fs.

articleTitle: Sparse and Composite Optical Lattices: Implications for Live Cell Imaging
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: New classes of optical lattices are described that yield large arrays of highly confined intensity maxima of selectable wavelength-normalized periodicity. Implications for high-speed, high-resolution live cell imaging and single molecule spectroscopy are discussed

articleTitle: Highly stable synchronized femtosecond Ti:sapphire laser with 1.3 W powers and sub-femtosecond timing jitter
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We realized stable synchronized femtosecond laser by coupling two 1.3 W mode-locking Ti:sapphire lasers with Kerr media, an ultra-long tolerance of length mismatch as 10/spl mu/m and timing jitter of sub-fs were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Long-range interactions in a cold Rydberg gas
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The excitation of cold Rydberg atoms is significantly influenced by long-range van der Waals interactions. Avoided crossings between interatomic potentials lead to molecular resonances, while energy level shifts from neighboring atoms suppress resonant Rydberg excitation.

articleTitle: Femtosecond hydrogen bond dynamics by spectrally- and time-resolved vibrational sum frequency generation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Time- and frequency-domain 3-wave mixing spectroscopy is developed as a surface-selective nonlinear technique capable of measuring spectral evolution of vibrational coherences. Hydrogen bond dynamics of interfacial water is observed to proceed on 100 fs timescale.

articleTitle: 100 μ J generation using a narrow linewidth Er+3-Yb+3doped fiber MOPA and its modeling
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on a narrow linewidth 100 muJ source based on 330 W peak power Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+3</sup>/Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+3</sup> fiber MOPA. Modeling including SBS and gain dynamic helps to optimize the amplifier architecture composed of fibers with different Brillouin shifts

articleTitle: Thermodynamic analysis of optical refrigeration in semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The cooling efficiency and optimum bandgap energy for semiconductor optical refrigeration are investigated from the standpoint of both the first and second laws of thermodynamics.

articleTitle: Optical coupling between spherical dielectric atoms
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: It is shown that dielectric microspheres with strongly detuned whispering gallery modes can be effectively coupled. The transition from strong to weak coupling is demonstrated as a function of separation between nonidentical microspheres.

articleTitle: Robust organic molecules with high optical nonlinearities and their use in hybrid microstructured optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The nonlinear optical properties of a new class of organic molecules with extraordinarily high third-order nonlinearities are presented. Their unique ability to be sublimated without decomposition is used to insert the molecules into microstructured fibers.

articleTitle: Chemical agent detection based on shaped laser pulse technology
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Binary phase shaping control based on multiphoton intrapulse interference of ultrashort pulses is coupled with time-of-flight mass spectrometry to provide a rigorous method for detection and identification of chemical agents in real-time.

articleTitle: Individual single wall carbon nanotube photonics
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Single carbon nanotube fluorescence spectroscopy was used to determine the emission lineshape. Nanotube fluorescence unexpectedly lacks intensity or spectral fluctuations resulting in a stable, single infrared photon source for exciting applications in quantum optics.

articleTitle: THz spectroscopy of excitons in bulk GaAs and in AlGaAs/GaAs quantum wells
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Distinctive excitonic spectral signature in Terahertz region provides an excellent method to probe the exciton population in semiconductors. We present the study of exciton formation and dynamics in GaAs bulk and quantum well systems.

articleTitle: Coherent coupling and optical manipulation of individual excitonic states
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present heterodyne detected transient four-wave mixing of individual exciton states. Coherent coupling between states is observed and single excitons are optically manipulated, driving their polarisation through a desired angle in the Bloch sphere.

articleTitle: Experimental Study for Low Resistance Interline Connections Using Pulsed Laser Techniques
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In this paper, experimental study was performed to evaluate the design of new four interline connect structures. The energy windows as well as optimal laser spot size were obtained from the experimental results, which show the minimum link resistance and highest yield. Accordingly above criteria, a best structure would be estimated

articleTitle: Intrinsic room temperature linewidth of CdSe/ZnS nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The temperature dependence of a single (ensemble weighted) CdSe/ZnS nanocrystal absorption linewidth is measured. The results are consistent with electron-optical phonon scattering as the dominant broadening mechanism at room temperature.

articleTitle: Mode Analysis and Modal Delay Measurement of Few Modes Fiber by using Optical Frequency Domain Reflectometry based on 1550 nm TLS
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The mode analysis and modal delay measurement based on the optical frequency domain reflectometry is suggested. Modal delay of few modes fiber is measured by OFDR and is compared with traditional pulse delay measurement method

articleTitle: Phase transition in the filament generation process in a Kerr medium
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We observed a phase transition in the rate of filament formation with increasing laser pulse power at the onset of conical emission from the filaments. Experimental and numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Quantum manipulation of a classical atom by a chirped microwave pulse
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: With a microwave pulse chirped from 19 to 13 GHz population in the Li n=70 states is transferred to the n=79 states through a phase locking of the electron's motion to the microwave field.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Pump-Probe Diagnostics of Preformed Plasma Channels
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report recent ultrafast pump-probe experiments in He plasma waveguides using intense pump and weak, same wavelength, cross-polarized probe. These single probe FDI measurements reveal otherwise undetectable weak blueshift, and depolarized component of pump

articleTitle: Super-resolved laser ranging using the Viterbi algorithm
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We adapt two-dimensional Viterbi algorithm for use with a ladar imager. We exploit line-of-sight and smoothness constraints to reduce complexity and extract axial object details much smaller than the temporal response time of the system.

articleTitle: Compact quasi-chaotic optical cavity
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a novel multi-pass optical cavity with partially-chaotic ray dynamics. For a centimeter-size device, our experimental measurements confirm meter-scale optical path lengths supported by the cavity, suggesting future applications in trace gas detection.

articleTitle: Nonlinear absorption spectrum in perylene derivatives
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Knowledge about nonlinear absorption spectra of materials used in photonic devices is of paramount importance in determining their optimum operation wavelengths. In this work, we have investigated the two-photon absorption (2PA) degenerate cross-section spectrum for perylene derivatives using the Z-scan technique with femtosecond laser pulses. All perylene derivatives studied present large 2PA cross-sections, only comparable to the best ones reported in the literature. The results achieved in the present investigation indicate perylene derivatives as promising materials for two-photon applications.

articleTitle: Population oscillations of two orthogonal states in a single quantum dot
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigated the exciton dynamics in a single self-assembled quantum dot with a V-type three-level structure. Using tailored pulse pairs we generated population oscillations between two orthogonal excitonic states without a direct transition.

articleTitle: Optical parametric generation properties of BiB/sub 3/O/sub 6/
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present detailed studies of the optical properties of the new nonlinear material BiB/sub 3/O/sub 6/ for parametric generation from the visible to near-infrared. We have determined the phase-matching conditions and effective nonlinear coefficients, acceptance bandwidths, spatial and temporal walkoff, and group velocity dispersion in the three principal optical planes. We also compare the properties of this material with /spl beta/-BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/, which indicate its potential advantages for parametric generation applications.

articleTitle: Single photon emission from gallium nitride quantum dots at a record-short wavelength of 357 nm
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present measurements of the second-order coherence function on emission from single GaN quantum dots. A large degree of photon antibunching is observed, demonstrating single-photon source operating at a record-short wavelength of 357 nm.
