articleTitle: Generation of efficient high harmonics in an orthogonally polarized two-color laser field
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Highly efficient high-harmonic generation was achieved in helium using an orthogonally polarized two-color laser field that consisted of the fundamental and second harmonic of a femtosecond Ti:sapphire laser. By applying a higher intensity second harmonic, the harmonics in the two-color field were stronger than those obtained in the fundamental field by more than two orders of magnitude. The conversion efficiency was as high as 5/spl times/10/sup -5/ for the 38/sup th/ harmonic at 21.6 nm.

articleTitle: A Method of Double Optical Modulation for Direct Combining Ethernet and Video Signals in Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We proposed a novel approach to enhance the data bandwidth by combining the optical Ethernet and video signals in a single wavelength. This technology could support a potential to wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) network applications

articleTitle: Atomic and molecular spectroscopy with a phase-locked, continuous-wave optical parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrated the phase-locking and continuous tuning capabilities of a continuous-wave, monolithic optical parametric oscillator (cw-OPO). At first, the cw-OPO was phase-locked to an optical frequency comb in the 830 nm region. The residual phase noise under phase-locking was 220 mrad in rms and the energy concentration to the carrier was 95%. Next, the signal light from the cw-OPO was phase-modulated by an external electrooptic modulator (EOM) in the microwave frequency. The single sideband was extracted by using a diffraction grating and a spatial filter. We could observe the Doppler broadened absorption and fluorescence profile of the Cs-D/sub 2/ line by tuning the signal wavelength to 852 nm and by scanning the microwave modulation frequency. We are trying the sub-Doppler spectroscopy of several atoms and molecules with the phase-locked cw-OPO and these results will also be presented.

articleTitle: Highly dispersive photonic crystal-based guiding structures
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Propagating modes supported by Photonic-Crystal guiding structures can demonstrate very high group velocity dispersion close to a cut-off. We investigate here the wavelength dependence of the dispersion for different Photonic Crystal structures.

articleTitle: Robust multi-partite multi-level quantum protocols
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present two three-level tripartite state quantum protocols. Utilization of the entangled mixed state shared between any two parties for quantum key distribution is shown. The realization using photon orbital angular momentum is discussed.

articleTitle: State-selective detection of ultracold rubidium molecules in high vibrational levels of the X /sup 1//spl Sigma//sub g//sup +/ ground state
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on state-selective detection of ultracold ground-state rubidium molecules in very high vibrational levels. Resonant two-photon ionization spectra obtained with a pulsed 600 nm laser are analyzed to identify the absolute vibrational quantum numbers.

articleTitle: Resonant optical transmission through a photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that a slab of photonic crystal can transmit 100% of an incident beam in the forbidden gap. This phenomenon is due to the resonant excitation of leaky modes along the interfaces.

articleTitle: Highly reproducible control of photofragmentation and ionization using binary phase shaping pulse
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Coherent control of photofragmentation and ionization process of a number of organic molecules following the excitation by binary phase shaped ultrashort laser pulses is presented. Results provide a highly reproducible tool for following different fragmentation pathways.

articleTitle: Resonant Tunneling Assisted Electroluminescence in InGaN/GaN Green LEDs with Nanocrater Structures
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Data are presented on the resonant-tunneling-related abrupt red shift observed in the temperature-dependent electroluminescence spectra of high-brightness InGaN/GaN multi-quantum-well green LEDs. It is found that the red shift arises mostly between 120 and 150 K, and brighter LEDs yield larger red shifts. These results are well explained by the proposed nanocrater model in which a Ga-rich quantum barrier surrounds the In-rich quantum-dot-like localized state. Intensity analysis manifests that the resonant tunneling from the quantum well to the nanocraters induces such an abrupt energy shift and enhances the room-temperature emission.

articleTitle: Variation of the carrier-envelope phase of few-cycle laser pulses due to the Gouy phase
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A simple solid-state-based approach is used to measure the variation of the carrier-envelope phase in the focus of a lens due to the Gouy phase. The experimental results are compared with analytical model calculations.

articleTitle: Chirality dependence of Raman cross-section in carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The chirality dependence for the cross-section of Raman scattering from the radial breathing mode of carbon nanotubes observed in recent experiments is explained using the empirical tight-binding method.

articleTitle: Femtosecond time-resolved mid-IR exciton Lyman spectroscopy of Cu/sub 2/O
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Kinetics of n=1 excitons are measured in Cu/sub 2/O using femtosecond time-resolved mid-IR spectroscopy. Observed density dependent ortho- to para-exciton conversion rate is attributed to a spin-exchange collision process, in good agreement with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Chirped RZ-DPSK modulation format in 40 Gb/s WDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have analyzed chirped RZ-DPSK modulation format for 40 Gb/s WDM transmission systems. We find that chirped RZ-DPSK improves 40 Gb/s WDM system performance by more than 2 dB as compared to regular RZ-DPSK modulation format.

articleTitle: Exact modeling of defect modes in photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An exact model for defect modes in PC devices with infinite cladding is presented. Its accuracy is demonstrated, as is its role in corroborating that the fundamental mode of a conventional PCF has no cutoff.

articleTitle: Calculation of power density directly from diffraction integrals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Direct intensity characterization from diffraction integrals is a promising technique for evaluating ultra-high field. The energy and momentum conservation for vector diffraction field are discussed to clarify the role of longitudinal field in the calculation.

articleTitle: Enhanced phonon-assisted absorption of InGaAs quantum dots confined in a planar microcavity
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: By utilizing photoluminescence excitation spectroscopy, we observed enhanced phonon-assisted absorption from InGaAs QDs confined in a planar microcavity. We also present the ability to couple two cavity modes through the phonon absorption and emission processes.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of soliton molecules
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Experimental investigations of temporal soliton molecules are reported. These molecules were recently discovered numerically; they consist of two bright solitons, glued together by a dark soliton, and exist only in dispersion-managed fiber.

articleTitle: Manifestation of inherent bandgap of photonic crystal in disorder-induced speckle pattern of scattered light
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Speckle pattern from disordered photonic crystal represents a sensitive tool for determination the stop-band width. We establish the quantitative relation between this width and the angular anisotropy of the intensity correlation function.

articleTitle: Polaronic signatures in intersubband transitions of strongly polar semiconductor heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Femtosecond two-color pump-probe experiments in the mid-infrared give the first evidence for a distinct optical phonon progression in the linear and nonlinear intersubband absorption spectra of electrons in a GaN/Al/sub 0.8/Ga/sub 0.2/N heterostructure.

articleTitle: Efficient Generation of Low-density Plasma Waveguides in Clustered Gases
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate waveguide generation for intense pulse guiding using end and side-pumped schemes. Up to 3times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup> Wcm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> pulses are guided in ~8 mm long argon plasma waveguides with little further ionization by the guided pulse

articleTitle: Relativistic kHz chirped-pulse amplified laser with >10/sup 8/ intensity contrast ratio and carrier-envelope phase stabilization
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a high-contrast relativistic kHz chirped-pulse amplified laser with carrier-envelope phase (CEP) stabilization. Contrast ratio of >10/sup 8/ and CEP stabilization with a jitter of /spl les/1 rad are achieved for laser pulses with relativistic intensity.

articleTitle: Development of a degenerate fermion chip trap
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present progress toward creation of degenerate Fermi gas of potassium-40 atoms trapped on a micro-fabricated chip. Such a cold quantum gas can be used to study low-dimensional many-body systems.

articleTitle: Simulation of coupling of ultra-intense laser pulses to funnel-mouthed plasma waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the results of simulations showing the formation of funnel-mouthed plasma channels in gas jets. Simulations then show 90% coupling efficiency of a 70 mJ, 100 fs pulse to the funnel-mouthed plasma channel

articleTitle: ASE-temporal contrast of 10/sup 10/ with a double CPA laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A double CPA Ti:sapphire laser system that includes two CPA stages with intermediate is non-linear temporal short pulse filtering is demonstrated. ASE temporal contrast of 10/sup 10/ achieved. The scheme is applicable to Petawatt power-level lasers.

articleTitle: Low-noise, efficient erbium-doped phosphosilicate fiber amplifiers extending to 1620 nm
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report 1570-1620 nm amplification using phosphosilicate EDFAs, achieving record-low noise figure of /spl les/5.5 dB at 2 dBm input, 27% overall power conversion efficiency with gain flattening (64% highest erbium coil PCE), and 22 dBm of output power.

articleTitle: Numerical aperture increasing lens microscopy for high resolution and high collection efficiency spectroscopy of single quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The numerical aperture increasing lens (NAIL) technique is applied to imaging and spectroscopy of single InGaAs quantum dots (QDs). Using NAIL, we demonstrate a resolution of 350 nm (/spl sim//spl lambda//3) and a six-fold collection efficiency increase.

articleTitle: Terahertz Fourier transform spectrometer based on a low-reflectivity Fabry-Perot interferometer
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A simple THz Fourier transform spectrometer is demonstrated by using a low-reflectivity Fabry-Perot Interferometer. The emission spectra of a wavelength-tunable photonic transmitter excited by an optical coherent control system are determined by the spectrometer.

articleTitle: Pulse compression in a silver gallium sulfide, mid-infrared, synchronously pumped optical parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Experiments and numerical modeling of optical pulse compression in a silver gallium sulfide synchronously pumped optical parametric oscillator show that compression depends strongly on the signal-idler group velocity difference.

articleTitle: Advances in Ti:Sapphire and Er fiber based femtosecond laser frequency comb systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Erbium doped fiber femtosecond lasers can efficiently be frequency doubled to 780 nm and subsequently broadened in a nonlinear fiber. Frequency combs created with such a setup may replace Ti:Sa lasers in frequency metrology applications.

articleTitle: Universality in depolarization through random scattering
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using a Mueller-Stokes analysis we measure the index of depolarization and the entropy of various scattering random media. We find excellent agreement with a recently predicted universality relation between those two parameters.

articleTitle: Molecular alignment, rotational wavepacket revivals and isotope separation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Following alignment by a strong femtosecond pulse, we observe multiple revivals of molecular rotational wavepackets in isotopic mixtures. Pronounced separation of isotopic signals and their interferences are demonstrated paving the way for a new isotope separation technique.

articleTitle: Light distribution from the analytical solution of the radiative transfer equation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An analytical expression of light distribution based on the analytical cumulant solution of the radiative transfer equation is presented. Time-resolved profiles obtained using the analytical expression are compared with the Monte Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: Finite pump beam size effects in optical-pump/THz-probe spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate effects of the finite pump beam size in optical-pump/THz probe measurements experimentally and numerically. A frequency-dependent size regime in which spectral distortion is minimal is identified and a correction method is presented.

articleTitle: Development of a high speed diode-laser-based ultraviolet absorption sensor for the hydroxyl radical
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Ultraviolet radiation is generated by sum-frequency mixing a distributed feedback laser and a diode-pumped solid-state laser to make high-speed absorption measurements of the hydroxyl radical. Measurements in a C/sub 2/H/sub 4/-air flame at 20 kHz are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Pyramidal targets as an advanced radiation source in laser-solid interactions
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A novel target design utilizing hollow pyramid geometry is studied as a radiation source of electrons, protons, and Ka X-rays. Experiments compare this source to flat foil and circular cone targets under similar laser conditions.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically induced transparency in rubidium vapor prepared by comb of short optical pulses
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We studied a propagation of comb of optical pulses produced by a mode-locked diode laser in rubidium vapor. EIT was observed when pulse repetition rate is subharmonic of the hyperfine splitting of the ground state.

articleTitle: Observation of the discrete Talbot effect
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the first observation of the discrete Talbot effect in one-dimensional waveguide arrays. Recurrence for different input patterns was observed in very good agreement with simulations. No recursion occurs for the zero diffraction direction.

articleTitle: Electron angular distribution from ultrahigh-intensity-laser and solid targets interaction
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An electron beam between laser-on-axis and target-normal direction and electron images at the target plate tangential direction are observed at rear and lateral side of the target. Two models are established to explain these phenomena.

articleTitle: Non-lithographic fabrication of polymer waveguides and grating couplers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Optical polymer waveguides were fabricated using a direct-dispensing technique. Grating couplers with deep grooves were fabricated by laser ablation. Optical measurements at a wavelength of 1.55mum gave a grating coupling efficiency close to 50%

articleTitle: Large reciprocal polarization rotation in planar chiral metal nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We observe large reciprocal rotation in quasi-2D chiral metal gratings. The effect originates from asymmetric coupling of surface modes centered at the air and substrate interfaces and violates neither reciprocity nor reversality of light-matter interaction.

articleTitle: Phase matching of X-waves in nonlinear crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The phase-matching conditions of interacting optical X waves in /spl chi//sup 2/ crystals are obtained. It is demonstrated experimentally that angular dispersion of the waves excited in optical parametric generator corresponds to angular dispersion of nondiffracting pulsed beams.

articleTitle: Effect of aggregated silver nanoparticles on spectroscopic properties of Eu doped Y/sub 2/O/sub 3/ powder
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have shown that luminescent properties of Eu:Y/sub 2/O/sub 3/ nanopowder can be influenced by aggregated silver nanoparticles. This demonstrates that spectroscopic properties of novel advanced random laser gain media can be engineered at nanoscale level.

articleTitle: Coherent acoustic phonons in silicon: propagation studies and imaging applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We generate and detect coherent acoustic phonon pulses in Si using ultrafast optics. A unified model of diffractive, dispersive, and nonlinear propagation effects is developed and verified. Imaging using diffracted phonon pulses shows submicron resolution.

articleTitle: Suppression of amplified optical parametric fluorescence in OPCPA
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The amplified optical parametric fluorescence (AOPF) from optical parametric chirped-pulse amplifier (OPCPA) was suppressed down to 5/spl times/10/sup 7/ with injecting a residual fundamental pulse of the seeded Q-switch Nd:YAG pumping laser as a quenching beam.

articleTitle: Double well potentials for atomic qubit gates in a designer optical lattice
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using four coherent laser beams we make two different 2D optical lattices with polarization-dependent periodicity. The lattices are coincident, and by shifting one with respect to the other, we create an array of double well potentials. We have designed a 2D optical lattice for /sup 87/Rb atoms consisting of an array of double well potentials. This lattice should allow us to test two-qubit gates and in general permit atomic control in support of nearest neighbor interaction physics such as the Ising model and quantum cellular automata.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Detection Sensitivity of Raman Spectroscopy by Utilizing the Effect of Light Localization in Microporous Structures
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a novel structure for a very efficient Raman spectroscopy detection of water contaminants. We experimentally prove the significance of light in this structure and demonstrate detection of nanomolar concentrations of pollutants

articleTitle: The Astra Gemini Project a high repetition rate dual beam petawatt laser facility
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: In July 2004 work started on a new dual-beam Ti:S PW laser facility at RAL. Intensities of between 10/sup 22/ and 10/sup 23/ Wcm/sup -2/ per beam are anticipated. We will describe this and the new science expected. A crucial aspect of the design is that the system will be capable of firing one shot per minute, offering a completely new experimental approach to ultra high intensity physics research.

articleTitle: Four-wave-mixing suppression in Er/sup 3+/ fiber amplifiers by backward pumping
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: By backward pumping of an erbium doped fiber amplifier additional spectral components resulting of four wave mixing outside the original pulse chirp were suppressed leading to a substantially improved recompression of the amplified signal.

articleTitle: Engineerable femtosecond pulses using aperiodic quasi-phasematched second-harmonic generation crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe a rapid method for exactly calculating the amplitude and phase of the pulses generated from any given input pulse in an arbitrary quasi-phasematched second-harmonic crystal.

articleTitle: THz pulse shaping and ellipticity control via optical rectification in nonlinear optical crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Pulse-shape and ellipticity of continuously tunable multi-cycle THz pulses are controlled by adjusting the relative time delay, intensity, and polarization between two femtosecond pulses. A THz wave plate using wire-grid polarizer also converts THz ellipticity.

articleTitle: Thermo-optic dispersion formula for BiB/sub 3/O/sub 6/
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Thermo-optic constants for BiB/sub 3/O/sub 6/ were measured from 20.0 to 120.0/spl deg/C at 0.5435 and 1.0642 /spl mu/m. The thermo-optic dispersion formula that reproduces well the temperature-dependent phase-matching conditions in the 0.3547-1.621 /spl mu/m is presented.

articleTitle: Atogram and nanometer trace element detection from solid surface by soft laser ablation atomic fluorescence spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Ultimate high sensitivity of trace element detection was proposed and demonstrated by solid surface analysis with laser ablation spectroscopy. Numerical calculation predicts LOD of atogram and 290ag was obtained experimentally about sodium in PMMA.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations and FROG measurements of 185 fs pulses generated from down-chirped dispersion-managed breathing-mode semiconductor mode-locked laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Balancing of spectral and temporal semiconductor gain dynamics allows broadening of mode-locked spectra. Our numerical model accurately describes SHG-FROG measurements of 185 fs pulses generated by down chirping of a dispersion-managed breathing-mode semiconductor mode-locked laser.

articleTitle: Excitation induced polarization decay in semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Excitation induced polarization dephasing in semiconductor quantum-dots is computed using a microscopic approach. The Coulomb interaction between localized and delocalized carriers leads to frequency dependent broadening and nonlinear resonance shifts. Non-Markovian effects are discussed.

articleTitle: Lasing and mode switching in circular Bragg nanoresonators
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate low-threshold lasing at telecommunications wavelengths from high quality circular semiconductor nanoresonators employing radial Bragg reflector single-mode emission and mode switching are observed at room temperature under optical pumping.

articleTitle: Theory of inducing electron spin coherence without spin precession in GaAs quantum well waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a theory for a differential transmission experiment that generated electron spin coherence in quantum well waveguides without DC magnetic fields. We show how optical selection rules explain the spin coherence's creation and detection.

articleTitle: Broadband Pulse Propagation with Electromagnetically Induced Transparency: Splitting of Adiabatic and Nonadiabatic Components
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The propagation of a broadband pulse through a dense resonant medium with a narrow transparency window is considered. We show that the pulse splits into a slowly propagating adiabatic part and a fast nonadiabatic part

articleTitle: Reshaping periodic light pulses by pulse multiplication
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a method for periodic optical pulse shaping based on superposition of time delayed, phase shifted, and weighted replicas of the original pulse train. The method is experimentally demonstrated using uniform fiber Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: A diode pumped, Nd:YAG, Q-switched unstable resonator developed for multi-billion shot, spaced based remote sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: This highly efficient Nd:YAG laser was designed as a prototype NASA-funded transmitter for space-based LIDAR missions. This design completed a 4.8 billion shot lifetest at 242 Hz with 10-15 mJ per pulse and 10 ns pulsewidth.

articleTitle: Compact chirped pulse optical parametric amplifier in periodically poled LiTaO3
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A compact chirped pulse optical parametric amplifier centered at 1064nm in periodically poled LiTaO3 was demonstrated. The total single pass gain of ∼10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>and ∼10.3% conversion efficiency were achieved in one OPA stage with low pump energy.

articleTitle: The performance of chip-scale atomic clocks
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We compare the performance of two chip-scale atomic clock physics packages, one based on excitation using the D/sub 2/ line of Cs and the other using the D/sub 1/ line of /sup 87/Rb.

articleTitle: Direct backward-emitted third-harmonic generation and its application to clinical microscopy
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Similar to forward-emitted third-harmonic-generation (THG), backward-emitted THG is found to be sensitive to interface inhomogeneity with improved longitudinal sectioning capability and can be applied to noninvasive clinical imaging.

articleTitle: CdTe quantum-dot doped glass for 1 Tbit/s all-optical switching
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Carrier recombination in CdTe quantum-dots is shown to be faster than 1ps without accumulation in long-lived states. Thermal effects influence absorption for times greater than 1ps. By eliminating those effects we demonstrate all-optical-switching at 1 Tbit/s.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Differential Phase-sensitive Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensor with Optimized Phase Extraction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A phase-sensitive surface plasmon resonance biosensor system optimized for accurate phase extraction and spurious signal removal is reported. We demonstrate that signal processing optimization is critically important for achieving 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>RIU accuracy.

articleTitle: Cascadability study of dispersion-compensated interleaver pairs for metro add/drop applications using a re-circulating loop
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A cascadability study is performed, using a re-circulating loop, of a 50-GHz-spaced dispersion-compensated interleaver pair. After five cascaded nodes, a 2.5-dB sensitivity differential is observed with /spl plusmn/0.07 nm wavelength detuning for with/without dispersion compensation pair.

articleTitle: Mode-locked ring lasers for the measurement of mirror backscattering
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: When a mirror is inserted at the pulse crossing point in a mode-locked ring laser, its beat note characteristic shows a dead band proportional to the backscattering coefficient, which can be as low as 10/sup -15/.

articleTitle: Single-mode vertical-cavity-surface-emitting-laser (VCSEL) with ring shaped microcavity and low divergence angle performance
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate 850 nm single-mode vertical-cavity-surface-emitting-lasers (VCSELs) with ring-shaped microcavity. Compared with the reported single-mode VCSELs, larger area of light-emitting aperture, smaller divergence angle of output beam, and lower resistance, have been achieved by our structure.

articleTitle: High-intensity Laser Induced Photo-proton Reactions
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time photo-proton nuclear reactions in various nuclei induced by a high-intensity, high repetition rate table-top laser and measure ratios of photo-proton/photoneutron cross-sections.

articleTitle: An optical decelerator for cold molecules
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a single stage optical Stark decelerator for neutral molecules which reduced the velocity of benzene molecules in a molecular beam by 25 m/s corresponding to a kinetic energy reduction of 15 %.

articleTitle: High-gain, polarization-preserving, Yb-doped fiber amplifier for low-duty-cycle pulse amplification
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An alignment-free, dual-pass, ytterbium-doped fiber amplifier with 25-dB gain and -44 dB noise floor is demonstrated for amplifying linearly polarized optical pulses with low duty cycle at a wavelength 23 nm off the gain peak.

articleTitle: Stopping, storing and releasing light in quantum well Bragg structures
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Stopping, storing and releasing of light in resonant photonic bandgap structures made from Bragg-spaced quantum wells is studied. The expected performance of almost ideal infinite systems is contrasted with that of existing structures.

articleTitle: Impact of laser frequency offset on DQPSK direct detection
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Frequency-offset impact on DQPSK direct detection is experimentally addressed with free-running sources. The heterodyned-measured frequency offset is related both with DQPSK BER performance and power penalty. Polarization-dependent delay impairment is isolated as well.

articleTitle: Optical nonlinearities of plasmons in single gold nanorods
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We measure third-order optical nonlinearities of plasmons in single chemically-synthesized gold nanorods using a novel interferometric scattering technique. We observe ultrafast, coherent material nonlinearities that are enhanced by localization of light in the rods.

articleTitle: Precision Rotation Sensing and Interferometry Using Slow Lght
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show how a combination of pulsed and CW excitation enhance the sensitivity of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and a Sagnac rotation sensor by the group index, which can be as high as ten million

articleTitle: Backward parametric oscillation in second-order nonlinear medium
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Following our new results on the generation of a backward THz wave by mixing two infrared laser beams in a GaSe crystal, we show that backward parametric oscillation is achievable in a few nonlinear crystals.

articleTitle: Photoporation and cell transfection using a violet diode laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Stable transfection of Chinese hamster ovary (CHO-K1) cells is achieved by photoporation with a violet diode laser. This represents the simplest method of laser-assisted cell poration reported to date

articleTitle: Intraband carrier relaxation in semiconductor quantum rods: competition between phonon-assisted cooling and Auger heating
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study intraband carrier dynamics in elongated CdSe nanocrystals and observe that in the high-intensity regime, carrier heating through Auger recombination becomes very efficient, leading to a significant slowing down of carrier cooling dynamics.

articleTitle: Photonic crystal quantum-dot laser with ultra-low threshold
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have fabricated L3-type photonic crystal microcavities with embedded InAs/GaAs quantum dots as active material. Single mode lasing has been found for devices emitting between 910-975 nm showing ultra-low lasing thresholds down to 160 nanoWatt.

articleTitle: Inducing electron spin coherence in GaAs quantum well waveguides: spin coherence without spin precession
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Electron spin coherence is induced via light-hole transitions in a quantum well waveguide without a DC magnetic field. The spin coherence is detected through effects of quantum interference in spectral domain nonlinear optical response.

articleTitle: Laser altimetry using pseudo-noise code modulated fiber lasers and photon counting detectors
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Laser altimeters using pulse code modulated fiber lasers and photon counting detectors appear to have attractive features for future airborne and space-based altimeter missions. We report some initial performance calculations and laboratory measurements using this technique.

articleTitle: Extraction efficiency enhancement in GaN-based light emitters grown on a holographically nano-patterned sapphire substrate
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We observed over two-fold enhancement in light extraction efficiency from GaN-based light emitters grown on a nano-patterned sapphire substrate. Nano-hole array patterns were generated by laser holography, which enabled a large area process with high throughput.

articleTitle: Arbitrary remote state preparation of photon polarization
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe the first experimental realization of arbitrary single-qubit remote state preparation. Specifically, a generalized measurement on one photon of a polarization-entangled pair conditionally prepares the remaining photon in an arbitrary desired state.

articleTitle: Coherent population transfer of ground state atoms into Rydberg states
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally and theoretically an efficiency of /spl sime/70%for excitation from the /sup 85/Rb 5S ground state to the 44D Rydberg state, using the technique of stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP).

articleTitle: Ultra-low time jitter pulse source using mode-locked fiber laser as a high-Q resonator
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Coupled opto-electronic oscillator, a ultra-low time jitter pulse source, can be modeled as a microwave oscillator with mode-locked laser (MLL) as a microwave resonator. The quality factor of the MLL was measured to be > 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>.

articleTitle: Comparison between Ge and InGaAs APDs in the 1 to 2 /spl mu/m wavelength range
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Ge and InGaAs avalanche photodiodes are suitable for lidar application at 1, 1.3 and 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelengths. A comparison between the two devices is presented, which addresses quantum efficiency, responsivity, dark current, noise and detectivity.

articleTitle: Slow light dynamics in warm rubidium vapor
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study slow light dynamics in Rb vapor cell. We present data showing significant pulse reshaping when the bandwidth of the pulses is increased. We present a model that qualitatively explains the observed behavior.

articleTitle: Optical rotation detection in a chiral scattering medium with an amplitude sensitive balanced detection polarimeter
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A amplitude sensitive balanced detection polarimeter is setup. The polarization gating and the spatial coherence gating enable to reduce the scattering effect The glucose concentration in a polystyrene microsphere scattering medium was measured successfully

articleTitle: Fast, widely tunable electro-optic Fabry-Perot filter
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A fast tunable Fabry-Perot etalon was developed using high performance OptoCeramic/sup /spl trade// PMN-PT. The response time fast than 500 ns was demonstrated. A dual-cavity tunable filter was designed and built, with a tuning range greater than 100 nm.

articleTitle: Cavity-waveguide interaction in photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate coupling between two photonic crystal cavities via a row defect waveguide. A coupled mode theory is then introduced to better describe cavity waveguide coupling near the waveguide band edge.

articleTitle: Fourier-synthesis of optical waveforms
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The talk will describe the generation of an optical pulse where the spectrum is sufficiently broad that the waveform is a single cycle in length, and where the temporal shape of this waveform may be synthesized. Specifically, we report the generation of a train of single-cycle optical pulses with a pulse width of 1.6 fs, a pulse separation of 11 fs, and a peak power of 1 MW. To synthesize a periodic waveform that is not sinusoidal, it is required that the radiation be phase coherent across its spectrum, and that the bandwidth of the radiation be large as compared to its central frequency. To obtain a multi-octave phase coherent spectrum, we use Q-switched laser pulses at 1.064 /spl mu/m and 807 nm to drive the fundamental vibrational transition in deuterium slightly off resonance. An essential ingredient of the work that is described here is the use of non-resonant four-wave frequency mixing in xenon as a diagnostic for the generated pulses.

articleTitle: Probing electrical signals in silicon CMOS devices using electric field induced second harmonic generation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the use of electric-field-induced second harmonic generation to investigate the electrical signal in a CMOS chip with 2.3 /spl mu/m femtosecond pulses. A linear relationship between the signal and electric field is found.

articleTitle: Tunable coherent microwave radiation by mixing two optical frequencies in a 47-mm-long GaSe crystal
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel approach for efficiently generating a monochromatic microwave tunable continuously in the range of 53-300 GHz by mixing two optical beams in a 47-mm-long GaSe crystal.

articleTitle: Impact of intrachannel crosstalk on the performance of direct-detection DPSK optical systems
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A method to assess the impact of intrachannel crosstalk on the performance of preamplified DPSK systems is presented. The 6 dB crosstalk tolerance relatively to OOK systems verified experimentally by Xiang Liu was analytically confirmed.

articleTitle: Novel automatic control for the optimum optical gain and phase difference in SOA-MZI wavelength converter
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have proposed and experimentally embodied the novel automatic control method for automatically adjusting and constantly maintaining the optimum optical gain and phase difference, to achieve the stable SOA-MZI wavelength converter with wide IPDR.

articleTitle: Phase space filling effects on exciton dynamics
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We model phase space filling effects in semiconductors excited via ultrashort optical pulses. We find that at high densities, groundstate excitons are strongly scattered into excited states, even in the absence of exciton-exciton interactions.

articleTitle: Generation of Doughnut-Like Beams by Means of a W-axicon Resonator with a Movable Axicon Element
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An optical resonator that generates doughnut-like laser beams is fabricated. A w-axicon with a movable center axicon enables us selecting any one of the Laguerre-Gaussian modes oscillation. Oscillation with a dye is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Wavelength-switchable fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A novel wavelength-switchable fiber ring laser with output selectable from one of 35 different wavelengths is reported. Wavelength variation of /spl sim/5 pm and power fluctuation of /spl sim/0.12 dB, were observed during a 2-hour stability test.

articleTitle: 50 to 350 GHz pulse bursts generation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on a passively mode-locked fiber laser source for optical pulse burst generation. The burst repetition rate was tuned from 50 to 350 GHz by 50 GHz steps only by changing the intra-cavity polarization.

articleTitle: Experimental multiphoton conditional state preparation and analysis
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A time-multiplexed detector capable of photon number resolution was used to investigate the photon statistics of a heralded photon source based on parametric downconversion in a quasi-phasematched KTP waveguide.

articleTitle: Optical control processes in terahertz quantum-cascade laser waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: An investigation of the optical control in the terahertz waveguide with quantum-cascade heterostructure is presented. Modulation in the waveguide is achieved by carrier plasma effect. In addition, we show an interaction of few cycle THz pulses with quantum cascade heterostructure.

articleTitle: High yield rep-rate operation of electra; an electron beam pumped KrF laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Electra has demonstrated high yield, 725 J, 1 Hz and 5 Hz operation for 100 second bursts. Analysis of fluorine dependence on yield shows replacing super-elastic collision processes with dissociative attachment processes improves agreement.

articleTitle: Terahertz spectroscopy of ultrafast demagnetization in ferromagnetic iron
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We use ultrafast terahertz transmission and emission spectroscopy to study ultrafast demagnetization in ferromagnetic iron. We show that demagnetization proceeds with a 1.7 ps/spl plusmn/0.3 ps lifetime in ferromagnetic films at room temperature.

articleTitle: Ceramic Nd:YAG split-disk laser amplifier with a 10 J output energy
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated a Nd:YAG split-disk amplifier. One pass gain and total stored energy were 2.0 and 11.1 J, respectively. The maximum output energy of 10.4 J was achieved at single-shot operation.

articleTitle: Quantum kinetics of phonon-assisted carrier transitions in semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Results for carrier-phonon scattering in semiconductor quantum dots are presented on the basis of a quantum-kinetic theory. In contrast to time-dependent perturbation theory fast capture and relaxation processes are obtained.

articleTitle: Modified spontaneous emission and qubit entanglement from two coupled quantum dots in a photonic crystal nanocavity
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Spontaneous emission dynamics of two dipole-coupled quantum dots in a photonic crystal nanocavity are theoretically investigated. Strong exciton-cavity coupling and dipole-dipole interactions are self-consistently incorporated and are shown to result in substantial qubit entanglement.

articleTitle: Increased polarization-entangled photon flux via thinner crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally that the production of polarization-entangled photons via type-II spontaneous parametric down-conversion is higher for thin nonlinear crystals than for thicker ones, basically because thinner crystals generate a broader spectrum.

articleTitle: Is the statistics of an amplified optical pulse in nonlinear semiconductor optical amplifiers Gaussian?
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: The Fokker-Planck approach is used to study the statistics of optical pulses propagating in semiconductor optical amplifiers where spontaneous emission dominates. The electric field is non-Gaussian for moderate and deep saturation levels.

articleTitle: Optical parametric processes in the presence of strong two-photon absorption
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Our experimental results indicate that the two-photon absorption sets the fundamental limits to optical parametric generation and oscillation in periodically-poled lithium niobate.

articleTitle: Theory of coherent dynamics in a quantum Hall system
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We discuss a theory of the coherent ultrafast nonlinear optical response of systems with strongly correlated ground states and show how the magnetoplasmon coherence in a Quantum Hall system affects the three-pulse four-wave mixing spectra.

articleTitle: Ultrafast manipulation of spins in antiferromagnetic materials
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using ultrafast laser pulses one can change the magnetic anisotropy of an antiferromagnet within 1 ps, allowing to manipulate their spins much faster than in ferromagnets. Possible direct optical spin manipulation will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Gain saturated operation of table-top soft X-ray lasers in neon-like ions at 5 Hz repetition rate
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the demonstration of gain saturated table-top soft X-ray lasers operating at 5 Hz repetition rate in Ne-like Ti at 32.6 nm and Ne-like V at 30.4 nm. Lasing was also observed in Ne-like Cr at 28.6 nm.

articleTitle: A numerically efficient semiconductor model with Fermi-Dirac thermalization dynamics (band-filling) for FDTD simulation of optoelectronic and photonic devices
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We describe a numerically efficient semiconductor model for FDTD simulation of optoelectronic and photonic devices that include the essential carrier dynamics such as band filling with Fermi-Dirac thermalization, spectral hole burning, and refractive index change.

articleTitle: Ultrafast X-ray measurements of inertial atomic-scale motion
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Using a new, accelerator-based source of femtosecond X-rays, we directly measure atomic displacements on an optically-modified potential energy surface. It is shown that the short time dynamics are predominantly inertial in character.

articleTitle: Joint polarization and spatial-mode entanglement of photons
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Simultaneous multidimensional entanglement can improve quantum communication protocols, measurements and fundamental studies. Using photons from parametric downconversion, we demonstrate a source of joint polarization and spatial-mode entanglement, and characterize the state by tomographic reconstruction.

articleTitle: Creation of a superradiance state by a sub-ps uni-polar half-cycle field pulse
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated that superradiance and superfluorescence states can be created in a selective manner in n=20 Rydberg states of Na atoms using a sub-ps, uni-polar half-cycle field pulse.

articleTitle: Highly efficient single-photon detection at communication wavelengths using upconversion in reverse proton exchanged PPLN waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrated single-photon detection at communication wavelengths with an overall system detection efficiency exceeding 46% using upconversion in a waveguide PPLN device in conjunction with a silicon-based single-photon counting module.

articleTitle: Experimental Observations of the Relativistic Deflection of Light
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Focusing several-cycle laser pulses to relativistic intensities in a lambda<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> volume on plasma of ~lambda scale-length leads to deflection of the radiation. Spatio-spectral measurements at I=1.5times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> show relativistic deflection and spectral broadening

articleTitle: Characterisation of multilayer dielectric gratings for petawatt-class lasers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a complete characterisation of multilayer dielectric gratings. We discuss on critical parameters for damage threshold studies, such as influence of pulse duration, number of shots on the grating, and incidence angle.

articleTitle: Fast spontaneous emission and slow light propagation in photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Two unique phenomena in photonic crystals are presented. One is the Purcell effect, which essentially enhances the spontaneous emission rate. The other is the slow light which is flexibly controlled by the photonic band engineering.

articleTitle: Electron and Proton Acceleration from Solid Targets by High-intensity Table-top Lasers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Electron and proton beams were investigated using a compact laser with intensities up to 2times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> irradiating thin targets. For the direction of the electron beam theory and experiment disagree

articleTitle: Periodic dispersion compensation induced by photo-sensitivity for achieving quasi-phase matching in holey fibers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: To achieve quasi-phase matching nonlinear process in one piece of holey fiber, a novel highly nonlinear holey fiber with doped photosensitive regions is proposed, which periodically compensates dispersion and phase mismatching in nonlinear interactions.

articleTitle: Generation of a nearly isolated high harmonic from a long capillary
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We generated a nearly isolated high harmonic in several-centimeter long capillaries filled with argon and studied the dependence of the selectivity of high harmonic generation on the pressure and gas species.

articleTitle: Entangling linear optics gates for Bell-state analysis and entangled cluster-state generation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We implement an entangling gate for photonic qubits that relies on a single interference condition, offering significantly improved gate fidelity, and describe its use for investigating optical cluster states and performing fully resolving Bell measurements.

articleTitle: Nd:glass regenerative amplifier with spatiotemporally shaped pulses for pumping an optical parametric chirped pulse amplification laser system
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present a Nd:glass regenerative amplifier which has been set up to efficiently pump an optical parametric chirped pulse amplification system. Spatial and temporal mode shaping of the pump pulse is described.

articleTitle: Counterfactual quantum computation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the first demonstration of Jozsa's "counterfactual computation", using an optical Grover's search algorithm. We put the algorithm in a superposition of "running" and "not-running", obtaining information even though the algorithm does not run.

articleTitle: Single-mode solid-state polymer dye laser fabricated with standard I-line UV lithography
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present single-mode solid-state polymer dye lasers fabricated with standard UV lithography. The lasers use a high-order Bragg grating and rely on index-tuning of a photosensitive polymer for waveguiding. The gain medium is Rhodamine 6G.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modes of a linear chain of nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We study numerically the dispersion relation and the structure of the optical modes along a chain of metallic nanoparticles. Polariton modes exists in both the radiative and non-radiative regions. Applications to nanophotonics are discussed.

articleTitle: SEM and SPM studies of single-shot damage on silicon
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Scanning probe microscopy was used to study femtosecond laser ablation of silicon as a function of laser wavelength, doping concentration, and sample temperature to gain a greater understanding of the femtosecond laser damage mechanism.

articleTitle: Large enhancement of fluorescence from CdSe/ZnS quantum dots induced by resonant coupling to spatially controlled surface plasmons
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Nanoengineered fluorescent response is reported in semiconductor core-shell (CdSe/ZnS) quantum dots in proximity to the surface plasmon field of periodic silver nanoparticle arrays. Tuning the surface plasmon resonance to the quantum dot exciton emission band results in an /spl sim/50-fold enhancement of the fluorescence.

articleTitle: The influence of nonlinearity, noise and extinction ratio on the cascading properties of 2R-regenerators
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have derived an expression for the BER of a cascade of 2R-regenerators including the effects of nonlinearity, noise and extinction-ratio. The best choice of threshold and the interplay between device parameters are investigated.

articleTitle: Using thermal profiling to quantify optical feedback into semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Thermal profiling is an ideal technique for monitoring optical feedback into semiconductor lasers in photonic integrated circuits. Quantitative measurements of optical output power, optical feedback magnitude, and threshold current shift are obtained without optical measurements.

articleTitle: Purcell factor enhanced scattering efficiency in silicon nanocrystal doped micro-cavities
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Scattering induced by nano-particles in a microcavity is investigated for the case of silicon nanocrystal doped microtoroids and a significant enhancement of scattering into the originally doubly-degenerate cavity eigenmodes is found, exceeding >99.42%.

articleTitle: Optical Carrier Wave Shocking: A parameter space analysis of the interplay between instantaneous and delayed material response
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We apply a recently developed pulse propagation technique (Pseudospectral Spatial Domain) to study the phenomenon of carrier wave shocking, which occurs when the process of self-phase modulation is accompanied by the generation of harmonics

articleTitle: True uni-directional pulse propagation using Fleck field variables
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Pulse propagation theories continue to ignore the backward-propagating field component. By using directional field variables, we derive wave equations allowing us to accurately judge the effect of the backward components

articleTitle: Temporal structure analysis of bright high-order harmonics obtained using self guided and chirped laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We performed an analysis on a phase-locked bright harmonic generation using self-guided and chirped laser pulses. In experiments, the bright harmonics were generated around the 61st harmonic from a long Ne gas jet in experiment. The theoretical analysis of the experimental results shows that emitted harmonics are locked in phase and form an attosecond pulse train with good synchronization.

articleTitle: Theory of spontaneously generated spin coherence in nanodots
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A physical picture of spontaneously generated spin coherence is given, based on the spin vector model. The theory underlying the experiment, which recently established this spontaneously generated coherence in a semiconductor nanodot is sketched.

articleTitle: Optically induced lattice dynamics probed with ultrafast X-ray diffraction
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We have studied the picosecond-dynamics of optically pumped hexagonal LuMnO/sub 3/ using ultrafast X-ray diffraction. Experimental data are compared with a simulation based on dynamical diffraction theory modified to account for the hexagonal structure of LuMnO/sub 3/.

articleTitle: Deterministically polarized fluorescence from single dye molecules aligned in liquid crystal host
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrated for the first time to our knowledge deterministically polarized fluorescence from single dye molecules. Planar aligned nematic liquid crystal hosts provide deterministic alignment of single dye molecules in a preferred direction.

articleTitle: Photon Statistics and Wave-Particle Correlations for an EIT System
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference

articleTitle: Skew reduction based on two-dimensional transmission gating using molecular dye film operated at 1.55 μm
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: All-optical pulse timing fluctuation reduction is successfully demonstrated using a film of organic molecular material, di(benzofuranonyl)methanolate, which is operated at 1.55 μm in an architecture using two-dimensional transmission gating.

articleTitle: Conditional generation of twin sub-Possionian states
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We conditionally generated quantum correlated sub-Possionian states with quantum correlation of 4.0/spl plusmn/0.2 dB between a pair of sub-Possionian states, which is exhibiting noise reduction of 4.0/spl plusmn/0.3 dB in intensity.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum Interference from Fresnel Diffraction Caused by Periodic Filamentation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Periodic filaments produced from diffraction were demonstrated in BK7 glass using femtosecond laser pulses. Stable ring and fringe patterns were observed and contributed to the interference of supercontinuum generation from these kind of periodic structure.

articleTitle: Polarization-preserving frequency conversion for high-efficiency photon counting and quantum communication
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report polarization-independent upconversion from infrared to visible wavelengths. This technique enables high-efficiency continuous-wave photon counting at 1.55 /spl mu/m, and is necessary for quantum-state frequency translation and long-distance teleportation.

articleTitle: Optical quasi crystals-properties and dynamics
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the first observation of wave dynamics in 2D Penrose-Tile quasi-periodic optical lattices, including experiments on linear "discrete" diffraction from various lattice sites, nonlinear (self-focusing) localization, and experiments on nonlinearly interacting quasi-periodic lattices.

articleTitle: Mapping the optical properties of SOI-type photonic crystal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on systematic mapping of transmission properties of W1 waveguides as a function of structural parameters. We demonstrate experimentally and theoretically that the bandwidth is maximized up to 120 nm by decreasing the hole radius.

articleTitle: Non-magnetic System with Negative Index of Refraction for Terahertz Application
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We propose a non-magnetic system with negative refraction index for terahertz applications. The system is based on a planar metallic waveguide with bismuth core, and uses strong anisotropy of bismuth permittivity and its ultra-low losses

articleTitle: Sub-10 ns Q-switched Yb-doped photonic crystal fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on a Q-switched fiber laser producing pulse durations well below 10 ns by using a short-length ytterbium-doped rod-type photonic crystal fiber as gain medium.

articleTitle: Performance of distributed fiber Raman amplifiers with incoherent pumping
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Distributed fiber Raman amplifier with incoherent pumping is investigated and the performance is compared to that with the conventional coherent pumping. Increasing the spectral bandwidth of incoherent pumping source will results in reduction of Raman gain linearly and gain ripple exponentially, and degradation of noise figure up to 1 dB, compared to coherent pumping with the same pump power.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal contrast of high-field laser
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We introduce a new concept of spatiotemporal contrast and demonstrate its relevance in experiments with high field lasers. Methods of mitigating effect of limited spatiotemporal contrast are discussed. Double-pass hollow-fiber cleaner for contrast improvement is proposed.

articleTitle: Probing nano-structures using Rayleigh scattering with supercontinuum radiation
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Rayleigh scattering using high-brightness sources provides a sensitive and general tool to probe the electronic properties of nano-sized structures. This capability is demonstrated by recording the electronic transitions of individual single-wall carbon nanotubes.

articleTitle: Engineered plasmon focusing on functional gratings
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report on the engineering of plasmon propagation and focusing by dedicated curved gratings and noncollinear phasematching. Gratings were created on gold by focused ion beam milling and plasmons were measured using phase sensitive PSTM.

articleTitle: Cubic phase distortion of single attosecond pulses being reflected on narrowband Mo/Si filtering mirrors
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We show that cubic phase distortion caused by narrowband Mo/Si multilayer filtering X-ray mirrors may considerably increase the time duration of single attosecond pulses.

articleTitle: High spectral efficiency scheme for optical label switching network
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: A novel high spectral efficiency scheme based on 40 Gb/s vestigial sideband modulation for all optical label switching is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. After label separation, the power penalties of payload and label are both less than 0.5 dB. It is shown that this method can effectively reduce the bandwidth of optical signal. In 40 Gb/s optical networks, the 20 dB bandwidth of payload combined with label is less than 0.54 nm. The influence of the wavelength difference between label and payload is also discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of correlated photons with conjugate pumps in a microstructure fiber
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We proposed and demonstrated a new method to generate correlated photons in a microstructure fiber via a reversed degenerate four-wave-mixing process with a pair of laser pulse at conjugate frequencies.

articleTitle: Anisotropy of gain in nanowire lasers
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigate the polarization properties of wurtzite GaN nanowire-based lasers. In particular, we emphasize the different orientations of the polarization of the lowest transitions in thick and thin nanowires.

articleTitle: Observation of modulational instability in photonic band gaps
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We present the experimental observation of modulational instability in 1D and 2D photonic lattices, at both the Brillouin zone base and edge. Edge dynamics lie in the spatial band gap and have no homogeneous counterpart.

articleTitle: Ghost interference with optical parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: 2005 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We analyze visibility loss in photon counting experiments with an optical parametric amplifier (OPA) source. The effect of the finite coincidence window time and bandwidth of the source is calculated for the Ghost interference experiment.
